content_units: With   $8,400 total balance   and   $700/month   available, your required minimums are   $255/month  , leaving   $445/month extra   to direct strategically.
-   Avalanche   = pays highest APR first → usually   lowest total interest
-   Snowball   = pays smallest balance first → usually   fastest psychological wins
-   Equal extra payments   = spreads extra across all cards → simplest, but usually not cheapest
- Interest estimated with monthly rates: APR ÷ 12
- Minimums held at the amounts you gave until a card is paid off
Strategy   How extra is allocated   Likely payoff order   Estimated payoff time   Interest efficiency
Avalanche   All extra to highest APR first   Card C → Card A → Card B   About 14 months     Best
Snowball   All extra to smallest balance first   Card C → Card A → Card B   About 14 months   Very close, but slightly worse than avalanche
Equal extra payments   Split extra across all three cards   All balances shrink together   About 15 months   Worst of the three
Because   Card C is both the smallest balance and the highest APR  , avalanche and snowball start the same way. The difference appears after Card C is gone:
-   Avalanche   next targets   Card A (24%)   before   Card B (18%)
-   Snowball   also happens to target   Card A   next because it is still the smaller balance

That means, for your specific balances,   avalanche and snowball are nearly identical early on   and may finish very close together. Still,   avalanche is the safer choice for minimizing interest   because it is mathematically optimal whenever payment discipline stays constant.
-   Card C minimum + all extra first
- Keep paying minimums on   Card A   and   Card B
- After   Card C   is paid off, roll its full payment into   Card A
- Then roll everything into   Card B
- It attacks the   29% APR   debt immediately
- It avoids letting the highest-interest card linger
- In your case, it also gives a quick early payoff on Card C

- Card C ≈   $0 to very small remainder range by next cycle
- If Card C still has a small residual balance after interest posts, nearly all of the   $480   finishes it
- Any leftover from that month can be redirected to   Card A
-   Card C is likely eliminated during Month 3
-   Card A becomes the next target immediately after
2.   Snowball   — extremely close in your case
3.   Equal extra payments   — likely costs noticeably more because Card C and Card A stay alive longer
-   Avalanche vs snowball:   probably only a   small difference
-   Avalanche vs equal split:   likely a   more meaningful savings  , because spreading extra slows payoff of the 29% and 24% balances
